topic.name: Integration Using Inverse Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions and Completing the Square

question.explanation:
First, we complete the square for the argument of the square root in the denominator: \[ \eqalign{ -x^2-4x & = -(x^2 + 4x)\\[5pt] & = -(x^2 + 2\cdot 2x + 2^2-2^2)\\[5pt] & = -((x+2)^2 - 4) \\[5pt] &= 4 - (x+2)^2 } \]

Substituting the above into the given integral, we get \begin{align*} \int \dfrac{1}{\left(x+2\right)\sqrt{-x^2-4x}} \textrm{d}x &= \int \dfrac{1}{(x+2)\sqrt { 4-(x+2)^2 } } \, \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int \dfrac{1}{2(x+2)\sqrt { 1-\left(\frac{x+2}{2}\right)^2 } } \, \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{4}\int \dfrac{1}{\left(\frac{x+2}{2}\right)\sqrt { 1-\left(\frac{x+2}{2}\right)^2 } } \, \textrm{d}x. \end{align*}

Let $u = \dfrac{x+2}{2}.$ Then, we have \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}=\dfrac{1}{2} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \textrm{d}x = 2\,\textrm{d}u. \]

Therefore,

\begin{eqnarray} \eqalign{ \newcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{\rm arsinh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{\rm arcosh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{\rm artanh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\sech}{\mathop{\rm sech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\csch}{\mathop{\rm csch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\coth}{\mathop{\rm coth}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{\rm arsech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{\rm arcsch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{\rm arcoth}\nolimits} \int \dfrac{1}{\left(x+2\right)\sqrt{-x^2-4x}} \textrm{d}x & = \dfrac{1}{4}\int \dfrac{1}{\left(\frac{x+2}{2}\right)\sqrt {1-\left(\frac{x+2}{2}\right)^2} } \, \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{4}\int \dfrac{1}{u\sqrt{1-u^2}} \cdot 2\, \textrm{d}u\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{2}\int \dfrac{1}{u\sqrt{1-u^2}} \,\textrm{d}u\\[5pt] & = -\dfrac{1}{2}\arsech u + C \\[5pt] & = -\dfrac{1}{2}\arsech\left(\dfrac{x+2}{2}\right) + C. } \end{eqnarray}

example.title: Completing the Square to Compute a Hyperbolic Arsecant Integral

question.explanation:
First, we complete the square for the argument of the square root in the denominator: \[ \eqalign{ -x^2-6x & = -(x^2 + 6x)\\[5pt] & = -(x^2 + 2\cdot 3x + 3^2-3^2)\\[5pt] & = -((x+3)^2 - 9) \\[5pt] &= 9 - (x+3)^2 } \]

Substituting the above into the given integral, we get \begin{align*} \int \dfrac{3}{\left(x+3\right)\sqrt{-x^2-6x}} \textrm{d}x &= \int \dfrac{3}{\left(x+3\right)\sqrt { 9-\left({x+3}\right)^2 } } \, \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int \dfrac{1}{\left(\frac{x+3}{3}\right)\sqrt { 9-9\left(\frac{x+3}{3}\right)^2 } } \, \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{3}\int \dfrac{1}{\left(\frac{x+3}{3}\right)\sqrt { 1-\left(\frac{x+3}{3}\right)^2 } } \, \textrm{d}x. \end{align*}

Let $u = \dfrac{x+3}{3}.$ Then, we have \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}=\dfrac{1}{3} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \textrm{d}x = 3\,\textrm{d}u. \]

Therefore,

\begin{eqnarray} \eqalign{ \newcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{\rm arsinh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{\rm arcosh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{\rm artanh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\sech}{\mathop{\rm sech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\csch}{\mathop{\rm csch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\coth}{\mathop{\rm coth}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{\rm arsech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{\rm arcsch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{\rm arcoth}\nolimits} \int \dfrac{3}{\left(x+3\right)\sqrt{-x^2-6x}} \textrm{d}x & = \dfrac{1}{3}\int \dfrac{1}{\left(\frac{x+3}{3}\right)\sqrt {1-\left(\frac{x+3}{3}\right)^2} } \, \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{3}\int \dfrac{1}{u\sqrt{1-u^2}} \cdot 3\,\textrm{d}u\\[5pt] & = \int \dfrac{1}{u\sqrt{1-u^2}} \,\textrm{d}u\\[5pt] & = -\arsech u + C \\[5pt] & = -\arsech\left(\dfrac{x+3}{3}\right) + C. } \end{eqnarray}

example.title: Completing the Square to Compute a Hyperbolic Arsecant Integral

question.explanation:
First, we complete the square for the argument of the square root in the denominator:

\begin{align*} x^2-10x+27 &= x^2 -2\cdot 5x + 5^2-5^2 + 27 \\[3pt] & = (x-5)^2 + 2 \end{align*}

Substituting the above into the given integral, we get \begin{align*} \int \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{|x-5|\sqrt{x^2-10x+27}} \,\textrm{d}x &= \int \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{|x-5|\sqrt {2+ (x-5)^2} } \, \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int \dfrac{1}{\left|\frac{x-5}{\sqrt{2}}\right|\sqrt{2+2\left(\frac{x-5}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2}} \, \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \int \dfrac{1}{\left|\frac{x-5}{\sqrt{2}}\right|\sqrt{1+\left(\frac{x-5}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2}} \, \textrm{d}x. \end{align*}

Let $u = \dfrac{x-5}{\sqrt{2}}.$ Then, we have \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \textrm{d}x = \sqrt{2}\,\textrm{d}u. \]

Therefore,

\begin{eqnarray} \eqalign{ \newcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{\rm arsinh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{\rm arcosh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{\rm artanh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\sech}{\mathop{\rm sech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\csch}{\mathop{\rm csch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\coth}{\mathop{\rm coth}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{\rm arsech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{\rm arcsch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{\rm arcoth}\nolimits} \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \int \dfrac{1}{\left|\frac{x-5}{\sqrt{2}}\right|\sqrt{1+\left(\frac{x-5}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2}} \textrm{d}x & = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \int \dfrac{1}{|u|\sqrt {1+u^2} } \cdot \sqrt{2} \, \textrm{d}u \\[5pt] & = \int \dfrac{1}{|u|\sqrt {1+u^2} } \, \textrm{d}u \\[5pt] & = - \arcsch u + C\\[5pt] & = - \arcsch\left(\dfrac{x-5}{\sqrt{2}}\right) + C. \\[5pt] } \end{eqnarray}

example.title: Completing the Square to Compute a Hyperbolic Arcosecant Integral

question.explanation:
First, we complete the square for the argument of the square root in the denominator:

\begin{align*} x^2+4x+5 &= x^2 +2\cdot 2x + 2^2-2^2 + 5 \\[3pt] & = (x+2)^2 + 1 \end{align*}

Substituting the above into the given integral, we get \[ \int -\dfrac{15}{|5x-10|\sqrt{x^2+4x+5}} \,\textrm{d}x = -\int \dfrac{15}{5|x+2|\sqrt {1+ (x+2)^2} } \, \textrm{d}x = -{3} \int \dfrac{1}{|x+2|\sqrt{1+(x+2)^2}} \, \textrm{d}x. \]

Let $u = x+2.$ Then, we have \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}=1 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \textrm{d}x = \textrm{d}u. \]

Therefore,

\begin{eqnarray} \eqalign{ \newcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{\rm arsinh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{\rm arcosh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{\rm artanh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\sech}{\mathop{\rm sech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\csch}{\mathop{\rm csch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\coth}{\mathop{\rm coth}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{\rm arsech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{\rm arcsch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{\rm arcoth}\nolimits} -{3} \int \dfrac{1}{|x+2|\sqrt{1+(x+2)^2}} \textrm{d}x & = -{3} \int \dfrac{1}{|u|\sqrt {1+u^2} } \, \textrm{d}u \\[5pt] & = {3}\arcsch u + C\\[5pt] & = {3}\arcsch(x+2) + C. \\[5pt] } \end{eqnarray}

example.title: Completing the Square to Compute a Hyperbolic Arcosecant Integral

question.explanation:
First, we note that \[ \int \dfrac{1}{16 - (3x+2)^2}\, \textrm{d}x =\int \dfrac{1}{16 - 16\left(\frac{1}{16}(3x+2)^2\right)}\, \textrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{16} \int \dfrac {1}{1- \left( \frac{1}{4}(3x+2) \right)^2}\, \textrm{d}x. \]

Let $u = \dfrac14 (3x+2).$ Then, we have

\[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}=\dfrac{3}{4} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \textrm{d}x = \dfrac{4}{3}\,\textrm{d}u. \]

Therefore,

\begin{align} \newcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{\rm arsinh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{\rm arcosh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{\rm artanh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\sech}{\mathop{\rm sech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\csch}{\mathop{\rm csch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\coth}{\mathop{\rm coth}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{\rm arsech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{\rm arcsch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{\rm arcoth}\nolimits} \dfrac{1}{16} \int \dfrac {1}{1- \left( \frac{1}{4}(3x+2)\right)^2 }\, \textrm{d}x & =\dfrac{1}{16}\int \dfrac{1}{1 - u^2 } \, \cdot \dfrac{4}{3}\,\textrm{d}u\\[5pt] & =\dfrac{1}{12}\cdot \arcoth u + C \\[5pt] & =\dfrac{1}{12} \arcoth\left(\dfrac{3x+2}4 \right) + C. \end{align}

Note that this result is subject to the condition $\left|\dfrac {3x+2}{4} \right| > 1. $
